extraction.Name: Oliver Morrisette
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 640 acre allotment at the time he got it, but was advised by the Indian Agency to take it, and he did so
extraction.Buyer: in 1922, sold 320 acres to Mr. Verncam, of White Clay, Nebraska, for $500.00 cash, and six head of horses, valued at $100.00 per head; in 1927, sold the other 320 acres to Henry Abold, of White Clay, Nebraska, for $70.00 cash, a team of horses, valued at $90.00 each, harness valued at $50.00, two cows valued at $100.00 each, a set of [harness?], and a Navajo blanket valued at $50.00
extraction.Occupation/Income: only income is derived from common labor
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; health is not good, being bothered with stomach trouble; has a wife and two minor children to support, all of whom have poor health, wife being especially frail; has never received any help from the County or Government; document dated November 19, 1928; allotment was 640 acres total, sold in two parcels of 320 acres each
